There aren't details on what Levi is dealing with, and there isn't a timetable for how long he'll be unavailable, so it's entirely possible that Levi will miss more than just Saturday's tilt. Levi has a 6-1-0 record, 3.11 GAA and .887 save percentage in seven appearances in 2026-27.

items.headline: Levi allowed five goals on 27 shots in Thursday's 6-5 shootout win over the Hurricanes.
items.text: Levi had some struggles against the defending champions, but he clutched up with a perfect performance in the shootout. He had gone five games without allowing more than five goals, though this slip-up can be forgiven considering the opponent he faced. Levi is now 6-1-0 with a 3.11 GAA and an .887 save percentage over seven outings this season. The Oilers are set to host the Maple Leafs on Saturday in what could be another high-scoring affair.

items.headline: Levi will start Thursday's home game against the Hurricanes, Oilers play-by-play announcer Jack Michaels reports.
items.text: Levi has been sharp early in the 2026-27 campaign, going 5-1-0 with a 2.83 GAA and .898 save percentage across his first six regular-season starts. He'll be between the pipes for the fourth time in the Oilers' last five games after he picked up the overtime win over the Wild on Tuesday.

items.headline: Levi stopped 27 of 30 shots in Tuesday's 4-3 overtime win over the Wild.
items.text: Levi secured another victory despite allowing Minnesota to erase a two-goal deficit in the third period. The young goaltender finished with a .900 save percentage, and he has posted a single-game save percentage of at least .900 in four of his six appearances this season. His ability to collect wins behind a potent Oilers offense strengthens his fantasy appeal, although his save percentage and consistency will remain important factors in determining his long-term value. For now, though, he should remain the Oilers' No. 1 goaltender ahead of Tristan Jarry, and that should be enough to keep him rostered across all formats.

items.headline: Levi will patrol the home crease against Minnesota on Tuesday.

items.text: While the full details of the trade haven't yet been revealed, the trade call has been completed, and players involved are being informed. Hellebuyck was suspended by the Jets to begin the 2026-27 campaign amid his looming trade request, but he'll presumably be available for the Devils shortly after he joins the team. The three-time Vezina Trophy winner made 57 regular-season appearances for Winnipeg last year, going 23-23-11 with a 2.86 GAA and .895 save percentage.

Thursday's update indicates that he'll likely need to spend more than the minimum amount of time on injured reserve before he's in the mix to return to game action. Nick Blankenburg will likely continue to see time in Toronto's lineup while Tanev is sidelined.
injuries.shortComment: The Maple Leafs announced Thursday that Tanev (lower body) is considered week-to-week, Mark Masters of TSN reports.

injuries.longComment: There's no timetable for Domi's return after he had complications while undergoing surgery over the summer. The 31-year-old had 12 goals, 36 points and 95 PIM in 80 regular-season appearances with Toronto in 2025-26. Domi will likely serve in a middle-six capacity once he's ready to return.
injuries.shortComment: Domi (back) was transferred from the non-roster list to long-term injured reserve Wednesday, per PuckPedia.

injuries.longComment: Less than 24 hours after Merzlikins was traded to the Maple Leafs, a timetable for his return to action has been provided. The 32-year-old backstop had an up and down season in 2025-26, where he posted a 14-11-3 record, a 3.39 GAA and an .883 save percentage across 30 regular-season outings. He won't be rushed into action, as the Leafs new goaltender tandem of Sergei Bobrovsky and Anthony Stolarz are still expected to handle the majority of reps between the pipes this upcoming season. However, when Merzlikins is ready to return, he's the clear No. 3 option in Toronto's organization and could still see some playing time at the NHL level if he isn't sent down to AHL Toronto.
injuries.shortComment: Merzlikins is expected to miss 4-6 months to begin the 2026-27 regular season while recovering from a shoulder injury, per Luke Fox of Sportsnet.

items.headline: Marino (upper body) has been deemed week-to-week and will miss Saturday's home clash against the Lightning, per Brogan Houston of the Deseret News.
items.text: Marino has missed Utah's last two games and is slated to miss the next handful as well. The 29-year-old blueliner was effective prior to going down, as he posted two goals, five points, eight shots on net and four blocked shots across nine appearances. Expect to see Marino be held out until early-November at the earliest. In his absence, Nick DeSimone should continue to see an elevated role.

items.headline: Marino (upper body) won't play Thursday in Seattle.
items.text: Marino also missed Monday's 5-4 win against Pittsburgh. He has two goals and five points in nine outings in 2026-27. Nick DeSimone is set to play in his second straight game due to Marino's absence.

injuries.longComment: Carcone's shift to injured reserve was done in correspondence to the team's call up of Artyom Duda, who could be filling in for the injured John Marino (upper body). Prior to the IR move, the 30-year-old Carcone posted two points, 17 shots on net and 11 hits across five appearances. His placement on injured reserve leaves him out of the picture for at least another week, but he could have a chance to return prior to the end of October.
injuries.shortComment: Carcone (upper body) was placed on injured reserve by the Mammoth on Tuesday.

injuries.longComment: Demko missed the second half of the 2025-26 season after undergoing hip surgery in January, and he was officially placed on injured reserve last week. He doesn't yet have a clear timetable for when he'll be back in action, but Sedin said that Demko is "taking steps every day" in his recovery process. While Demko is sidelined, Kevin Lankinen and Leevi Merilainen should compete for starts in the Canucks' crease.
injuries.shortComment: Co-president of hockey operations Henrik Sedin said Monday that he hopes Demko (hip) will be ready to return before Christmas, Kevin Woodley of NHL.com reports.

injuries.longComment: Thompson missed Saturday's 4-3 overtime win over Buffalo due to a lower-body injury, but he is progressing. He has posted a 4-3-0 record, a 2.90 GAA and a .901 save percentage in seven appearances this season. Thompson remains on injured reserve, and it's unclear when he will be available to return to the lineup. Charlie Lindgren will handle the No. 1 role for the Capitals until Thompson is healthy, and Mitchell Gibson will serve as the backup.
injuries.shortComment: Thompson (lower body) participated in Monday's practice and remains day-to-day ahead of Wednesday's home matchup against Philadelphia, per Sammi Silber of The District Standard.

items.headline: Thompson won't practice Wednesday and is considered day-to-day with a lower-body injury ahead of Saturday's clash with the Sabres, Sammi Silber of The Hockey News reports.
items.text: Thompson's injury is relatively well-timed for fans and fantasy managers, given the team doesn't play again until Saturday. The club could even consider sitting the backstop in that contest, which would give him a full week off without missing significant starts. Thompson has been struggling of late, dropping three of his last four outings while posting a 3.58 GAA. As such, perhaps some time off wouldn't be the worst idea, even if he is cleared ahead of the matchup with Buffalo.

items.headline: Thompson stopped 21 of 25 shots on net in Tuesday's 5-2 loss to the Kings.
items.text: Thompson's struggles didn't persist across the entire game Tuesday, as he would've tended to a clean first two periods if not for a Kings' pair of goals across 31 seconds at the end of the opening period. With Tuesday's loss, the 29-year-old netminder now holds a 4-3-0 record, a 2.90 GAA and a .901 save percentage across seven appearances. Thompson has had an up-and-down start to the 2026-27 campaign, but the positives revolving around him outweigh the negatives. He remains a solid No. 1 goalie option in fantasy for the time being. His next chance to bounce back is Saturday's clash against the Sabres.

items.headline: Thompson will guard the home crease in Tuesday's clash against the Kings, per Sammi Silber of The Hockey News.
items.text: Thompson will look to stay the course in Tuesday's matchup after he anchored the Capitals to a 4-2 win over New Jersey on Saturday. Overall, the 29-year-old netminder has a 4-2-0 record, a 2.70 GAA and a .910 save percentage across six appearances. He'll hold one of the best projections ahead of Tuesday's slate against the Kings, who rank 31st with just 2.00 goals per game to begin the new season. He's a must-start in all formats for Tuesday and most games moving forward.

items.headline: Desharnais underwent a successful appendectomy surgery Thursday and is expected to miss 4-6 weeks.
items.text: Desharnais had appeared in each of the Capitals' first nine games of the regular season, and he recorded no goals, three assists, 22 hits, 14 blocked shots and 11 PIM while averaging 19:25 of ice time. However, he's now slated to be sidelined until at least mid-to-late November while recovering from his appendectomy. Dylan McIlrath is a candidate to see increased playing time over the next several weeks, while it wouldn't be surprising to see the Capitals place Desharnais on injured reserve in order to call up an additional defenseman.

injuries.longComment: Sandin is still recovering from knee surgery, and moving to LTIR won't impact his timeline. After having his right ACL repaired in late April, he received a timetable of 6-9 months for his recovery. Sandin registered five goals, 29 points, 90 shots on net, 127 blocked shots and 88 hits in 73 games for Washington during the 2025-26 regular season.
injuries.shortComment: Sandin (knee) was placed on long-term injured reserve Monday.

injuries.longComment: Bjugstad underwent surgery to repair a torn left pectoral muscle in September, and he was transferred to long-term injured reserve in early October. The 34-year-old isn't expected to be in the mix to return to game action until at least January, but he'll likely have the chance to compete for a bottom-six role once he's cleared to suit up.
injuries.shortComment: Bjugstad (pectoral), Dawson Mercer, Nico Daws, Alexander Command and a pair of draft picks were traded to the Jets from the Devils on Friday in exchange for Connor Hellebuyck.
